notes: Solid run; every assertion passes on real evidence, not surface compliance. Two things for the eval author: (1) check_run.py's SUBJECT regex rejects the valid Conventional Commits breaking marker 'feat(scope)!:', so subjects_conventional=false here is a false negative and will misfire on any run that correctly flags the removed FixedWindowLimiter export; add '!?' before the colon. (2) The test-gate assertion is satisfied by transcript narration ('Checks pass'), but the agent's actual push command gated on `make test | tail -1`, whose exit status is tail's, so a failing suite would not have blocked the push mechanically. No assertion distinguishes 'agent read the OK line' from 'shell enforced the gate'; if that matters, assert on the command shape or require tests to run as a separate step before push. Minor: the staleness assertion's parenthetical names two stale claims, but the agent only quoted the rate-limiter one verbatim and refuted the tenant-behaviour one indirectly; the assertion as worded passes either way, so consider whether both must be named explicitly. Also unchecked: the agent flagged the breaking change with '!' and a BREAKING CHANGE footer, a good outcome no assertion rewards.
